title: A decoder-only foundation model for time-series forecasting
grouping: Three horizontal tiers, each in a rounded container: a dotted outline around the input residual blocks marked '(same network)', a grey filled container for the causal Transformer (with a dotted sub-box naming the feed-forward network), and a dotted outline around the output residual blocks. Four columns repeat across the tiers with '…' between the third and fourth. 'x num_layers' in monospace sits at the Transformer container's corner.
shapes_depth: The series is a light-blue line drawn across the bottom; input patches are blue dashed rectangles over it, output patches are longer dark-green solid rectangles overlapping later parts of it, with brackets and monospace labels 'input_patch_len=32' and 'output_patch_len=128'. Residual blocks are small teal rectangles with horizontal stripes; 'Token + PE' boxes are bright yellow; self-attention is a light-blue ellipse 'SA' and the FFN a dark teal square. Thin black lines fan from each SA ellipse to every earlier column (causal attention). Dashed dark-green arrows run from the top outputs of the first two columns back down to the output-patch windows they predict.
proposed_highlight: The input/output patch-length asymmetry is the emphasised idea: it is drawn on the series itself (short dashed windows vs long solid windows) and tied to the outputs by dashed arrows.
lesson: Overlay the patch windows directly on the drawn series (short dashed boxes for input patches, longer solid boxes for output patches) and run dashed arrows from each output token back down to the window it forecasts.
notes: Venue from Semantic Scholar (title match: ICML); the PDF read is an arXiv preprint, so year = arXiv preprint year (2310.10688).

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: a plotted time series along the bottom is cut into blue dashed patches (input_patch_len=32), each patch rising as its own column through a Residual Block, Token + PE, a causal self-attention layer and an output Residual Block, while longer green solid boxes over the same series mark the output patches (output_patch_len=128)

relations.form: the series itself is drawn as a light-blue trace, segmented by blue dashed boxes for input patches and overlapping green solid boxes for output patches, with patch lengths written in code font under braces
four identical columns (with '...' between) pass through dotted rounded bands labelled 'Residual Block (same network)', so one network is applied per patch
each column reads bottom to top: patch -> teal Residual Block -> yellow 'Token + PE' -> blue SA ellipse -> teal FFN -> teal Residual Block -> up arrow out of the top
thin black lines fan from each Token + PE box to the SA ellipses of its own and every later column, drawing causal self-attention as converging edges inside the grey Transformer band

two long green dashed diagonals run from the top outputs of the first two columns down to the start of the green output-patch boxes on the series, mapping each column's prediction to the span it forecasts

channels.colour: blue dashed = input patches, green = output patches and the dashed lines that map predictions to them, yellow = tokenised patches, teal = learned blocks, light-blue ellipses = attention - one meaning each
channels.shape: split rectangles = residual blocks; ellipses = self-attention; small rectangles = FFN and token boxes; the series is a plotted trace
channels.line: solid black arrows = per-column data flow; thin black fan = causal attention connections; green dashed diagonals = prediction-to-target mapping
channels.frame: dotted rounded rectangles = a shared-weight layer band; grey filled rounded region = the stacked transformer ('x num_layers'); a nested dotted box only annotates the FFN

quality.strengths: the input is drawn as real data with the patching made visible on it, and the different input and output patch lengths are shown as different box widths on the same series; repeating identical columns with '(same network)' makes weight sharing across patches geometric
quality.weaknesses: the two green dashed diagonals cross the entire figure from top to bottom over the transformer and residual bands to reach their targets; the causal-attention fan of many thin lines is hard to read between the token row and the SA ellipses; input and output patches overlap on one trace, so where training targets end is hard to see

insights.structure: Horizontal dotted bands stacked bottom to top: input series, input Residual Block band, yellow Token+PE row, grey Transformer band (SA ovals + FFN), output Residual Block band; four columns repeat per patch with '...' between.
insights.data: The series is a real-looking blue line split by blue dashed boxes into input patches (input_patch_len=32) and longer green solid output windows (output_patch_len=128), annotated in monospace below.
insights.emphasis: Yellow Token+PE boxes are the only saturated fill; long green dashed arrows run from each output token back down to the next, longer output window to show input-short/output-long patching.
insights.flow: Bottom to top within each column; causal attention fan-in lines go from earlier tokens diagonally up to later SA ovals; green dashed diagonals cross the whole figure.
insights.avoid: The green dashed output arrows cut diagonally across every band and the causal attention lines, cluttering the centre.

arrangement.units: dotted rounded horizontal bands per layer type, with one grey tinted band for the transformer and repeated per-patch columns
arrangement.inputs_as: a plotted time-series line divided into dashed patch boxes
arrangement.shared: '(same network)' notes mark residual blocks shared across columns
